oligos.oligo_name: Defibrotide, porcine-derived active pharmaceutical ingredient (branded formulation)
oligos.aliases: porcine defibrotide; defibrotide sodium; polydeoxyribonucleotide sodium salt; branded/Gentium material
oligos.indication: post-haematopoietic stem cell transplant hepatic veno-occlusive disease (VOD) / sinusoidal obstruction syndrome (SOS)
oligos.max_phase: Approved (this is the marketed branded material; the source calls it 'the branded formulation')
oligos.sequence_locus: NOT_APPLICABLE - polydisperse mixture of natural porcine intestinal mucosal DNA fragments; no sequence is printed anywhere in the article and none can exist for a batch-level material
oligos.sugar_modifications: 2'-deoxyribose (natural DNA); no synthetic sugar modification reported
oligos.ps_count: 0 (source states the material is phosphodiester; this is an affirmed zero, not a missing value)
oligos.identity_confirmation: Size exclusion chromatography (Waters HPLC, tandem PSK 2000/3000 columns, heparin molecular fractions 2000-50,000 as calibrators): mean weighted MW 18.02 +/- 0.32 kDa (Table 7). DNA content by Heparin Red fluorescence: 79 +/- 6.39 ug per 10 ug API (Table 6).
oligos.synthesis_platform: Controlled depolymerisation of porcine intestinal mucosal DNA (natural extraction, byproduct of heparin manufacture); not solid-phase oligonucleotide synthesis
oligos.notes: Batch-level material, NOT a defined sequence: 19 independent porcine API production lots analysed, each with its own manufacturer reference number. Backbone assigned full_PO from the source's own words: 'It consists of a mixture of single-stranded (90%) and double-stranded (10%) phosphodiester oligonucleotides' (Introduction). No synthetic phosphorothioate or sugar modification is described anywhere in either source; defibrotide is extracted natural DNA, not solid-phase synthesised. Composition per source: 90% single-stranded / 10% double-stranded phosphodiester oligonucleotides. Same material class as DEFITELIO in S19 (Gentium S.r.L. appears as a DEFITELIO establishment in the SPL), but kept as a separate oligo key because S4 measured its own API lots and the two sources report different MW figures.

oligos.oligo_name: Defibrotide, ovine-derived active pharmaceutical ingredient (research grade)
oligos.aliases: ovine defibrotide; sheep-derived defibrotide; generic ovine defibrotide API
oligos.indication: investigational alternative source material for the same VOD/SOS indication as porcine defibrotide
oligos.max_phase: Preclinical / research-grade API - source states 'At the time of this study, no FDA-approved or commercially available generic ovine defibrotide formulation available.'
oligos.sequence_locus: NOT_APPLICABLE - polydisperse mixture of natural ovine intestinal mucosal DNA fragments; no sequence printed
oligos.sugar_modifications: 2'-deoxyribose (natural DNA); no synthetic sugar modification reported
oligos.ps_count: 0 (phosphodiester material per source; affirmed zero, not a missing value)
oligos.identity_confirmation: Size exclusion chromatography as above: mean weighted MW 16.8 +/- 0.24 kDa (Table 7). DNA content by Heparin Red fluorescence: 75.78 +/- 4.74 ug per 10 ug API (Table 6).
oligos.synthesis_platform: Byproduct of ovine heparin manufacture from ovine intestinal mucosa; natural extraction, not solid-phase synthesis
oligos.notes: Batch-level material: 9 independent ovine API production lots. Backbone assigned full_PO from the source's own words: 'It consists of a mixture of single-stranded (90%) and double-stranded (10%) phosphodiester oligonucleotides' (Introduction). No synthetic phosphorothioate or sugar modification is described anywhere in either source; defibrotide is extracted natural DNA, not solid-phase synthesised. The phosphodiester/ss-ds composition statement in the Introduction is written about defibrotide generically and is cited to reference 4/14 (porcine material); the article does not separately chemically characterise the ovine backbone, so full_PO for the ovine lots is carried over from that generic statement plus the shared DNA-extraction manufacturing route. Flagged for reviewer.

oligos.aliases: DEFITELIO; defibrotide sodium; polydeoxyribonucleotide, sodium salt; defibrotide free acid
oligos.indication: Treatment of adult and pediatric patients with hepatic veno-occlusive disease (VOD) with renal or pulmonary dysfunction following HSCT
oligos.developer: Jazz Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (labeler); manufacturing establishments include Gentium S.r.L and Patheon Italia S.p.A.

oligos.ps_count: NOT_REPORTED - the label states 'polydeoxyribonucleotide, sodium salt' but never names the internucleotide linkage chemistry in text
oligos.identity_confirmation: Label states mean weighted molecular weight of 14-19 kDa and 'a potency of 27-39 and 28-38 biological units per mg as determined by two separate assays measuring the release of a product formed by contact between defibrotide sodium, plasmin and a plasmin substrate' (Section 11).

measurements.verbatim_quote: In the 13-week toxicity studies in rats and dogs, intravenous administration of defibrotide sodium transiently prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT) at 1200 and 4800 mg/kg/day administered as a continuous infusion in rats and at 300 and 1600 mg/kg/day administered in 2-hour infusions 4 times daily in dogs. Prothrombin time (PT) was also transiently increased at 4800 mg/kg/day in rats. These findings were observed at doses at least 6 times higher on a mg/m2 basis than the clinical dose of 25 mg/kg/day. The effects on APTT and PT may be due to direct effects on coagulation based on the dose-dependent response observed.
measurements.notes: Dose-resolved but value-free: the label names the dose levels at which the change occurred and never prints a clotting time. readout_value is NOT_REPORTED and readout_is_qualitative is true accordingly - no number was invented. Both flags true: coagulation modulation is on-target pharmacology for defibrotide, and this is simultaneously a toxicology finding at supratherapeutic exposure. The label supplies the causal attribution itself: 'The effects on APTT and PT may be due to direct effects on coagulation based on the dose-dependent response observed.' Note the label reports the clinical comparator as 25 mg/kg/day, which is the 6.25 mg/kg q6h regimen of Section 2.1 expressed as a daily total. The 4800 mg/kg/day rat level appears in both an aPTT row and the PT row - one dose, two readouts, not a duplicate.

measurements.source_locus: Section 12.1 Mechanism of Action
measurements.verbatim_quote: The mechanism of action of defibrotide sodium has not been fully elucidated. In vitro, defibrotide sodium enhances the enzymatic activity of plasmin to hydrolyze fibrin clots. Studies evaluating the pharmacological effects of defibrotide sodium on endothelial cells (ECs) were conducted primarily in the human microvascular endothelial cell line. In vitro, defibrotide sodium increased tissue plasminogen activator (t-PA) and thrombomodulin expression, and decreased von Willebrand factor (vWF) and plasminogen activator inhibitor‑1 (PAI-1) expression, thereby reducing EC activation and increasing EC‑mediated fibrinolysis.
measurements.notes: Qualitative mechanistic row: direction is stated by the label, magnitude is not. Included because fibrinolysis markers (t-PA, PAI-1, plasmin) and vWF/thrombomodulin are coagulation-cascade readouts within this endpoint's scope. vWF and thrombomodulin are reported as EXPRESSION in endothelial cells, not as plasma factor activity - do not treat them as factor-activity assays.

measurements.source_locus: Section 12.2 Pharmacodynamics, 'PAI-1 Inhibition' subsection
measurements.verbatim_quote: Plasma concentrations of PAI-1 were assessed on an exploratory basis as a potential pharmacodynamic marker for efficacy in Study 2. PAI-1 is an inhibitor of t-PA and therefore of fibrinolysis. extraction_notes:
SCOPE AND SHAPE. Defibrotide is curated as a batch-level polydisperse ssDNA material, not a defined sequence: sequence fields are NOT_APPLICABLE on all three oligo records and sequences_captured is 0. The modifications array is deliberately EMPTY - neither source publishes per-position chemistry, and for a polydisperse natural-DNA mixture per-position chemistry cannot exist. Nothing was modelled.

S19's Section 11 says 'The primary structure of defibrotide sodium is shown below' and then embeds a chemical-structure IMAGE (renderMultiMedia ID_8eb51eb5-786b-4dd9-9c67-d5a2caf78746). No sequence was read from that image and none is recorded.

S4 HAZARD 1 - ANTI-Xa / ANTI-IIa UNITS ARE INTERNALLY CONTRADICTORY. Tables 4 and 5 head the value column 'Time (sec)' and the Results narrative repeats '7.44 ± 2.70 s', but the Methods define the expected unexposed baseline as 'near zero (below 5%)', i.e. a percentage, and the assay is amidolytic (chromogenic), which does not yield seconds. readout_unit is recorded as 's' because that is what the source prints; a reviewer MUST resolve the unit before these four rows are compared against any other compound. This is the only anti-Xa/anti-IIa data in the whole union, so the defect matters.

S4 HAZARD 2 - DUPLICATED VALUES. (a) The ovine value 7.44 +/- 2.70 is printed identically for anti-Xa (Table 4) and anti-IIa (Table 5). (b) The porcine aPTT mean 39.74 is printed identically in Table 1 (whole blood, SD 2.60) and Table 3 (blood bank plasma, SD 2.57). Both look like transcription duplications in the source. Everything is transcribed as printed; nothing was corrected or dropped.

S4 HAZARD 3 - INTERPRETATION vs REFERENCE RANGE. The Methods quote aPTT normal 26-38 s and TT normal 14-21 s. Porcine aPTT is 39.74 s in two matrices, ABOVE the stated aPTT range, yet the source concludes 'no anticoagulation effect' in aPTT; conversely porcine whole-blood TT is 20.42 s, INSIDE the stated TT range, yet the source concludes a 'mild anticoagulant effect' in TT. effect_direction follows the SOURCE'S stated interpretation in every case and the arithmetic conflict is flagged on each affected row.

S4 HAZARD 4 - NO UNTREATED CONTROL. 'untreated control samples were not included'. Every S4 row therefore has control_value NOT_REPORTED; the only comparison the source itself makes is ovine vs porcine. No treated-vs-baseline delta or percent-of-control was computed.

S4 HAZARD 5 - ABSTRACT vs METHODS CONTRADICTION. The Abstract says the API was 'added to pooled plasma and whole blood', while the Methods say 'Plasma obtained from healthy volunteer donors was processed and analyzed individually and was not pooled across donors.' The Methods wording is used in system_model. Unresolved in the source.

S4 - n IS BATCHES, NOT SUBJECTS. n_subjects carries '19 independent porcine API batches' / '9 independent ovine API batches'. These are production lots; the number of blood donors is never stated. Do not treat n as a biological replicate count.

S4 - FIGURES NOT DIGITISED. Figures 1-6 plot the same data as Tables 1-7 (Figure legends say mean +/- SD, Results says figures 'display the mean and standard errors'). Every S4 number here comes from the machine-readable JATS <table> elements and is corroborated by the Results narrative text. Nothing was read off a figure image.

S19 - DOSE-RESOLVED BUT VALUE-FREE. Section 13.2 names the exact dose levels at which APTT and PT changed in rats and dogs but prints no clotting times, no group means and no NOAEL. Those five rows carry readout_value NOT_REPORTED with readout_is_qualitative true. The label supplies its own causal attribution ('may be due to direct effects on coagulation based on the dose-dependent response observed') and its own safety multiple ('at least 6 times higher on a mg/m2 basis than the clinical dose of 25 mg/kg/day'), both quoted verbatim.

S19 - DENOMINATOR HAZARD. Section 6.1 uses n=176 for the overall and Table 2 incidences but n=102 for the permanent-discontinuation incidences. The two sets of percentages are NOT comparable and must not be pooled. Flagged on every discontinuation row.

S19 - REPORTING RULE CONDITIONS THE INCIDENCES. 'events were not required to be reported if they were related to the hepatic VOD, or if they were expected to occur after hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation (HSCT), unless they were serious or Grade 4-5'. Bleeding incidences are therefore under-ascertained by design, and patients with significant acute bleeding at entry were excluded. Table 2's inclusion rule ('>=10% any grade or Grade 4/5 >=2%') also means a bleeding site absent from Table 2 is not a zero.

S19 - PAI-1 APPEARS TWICE WITH OPPOSITE OUTCOMES. Section 12.1 reports decreased PAI-1 EXPRESSION in vitro (direction: decrease); Section 12.2 reports a clinical PLASMA PAI-1 null (direction: no_change, 'did not reach statistical significance'). Two separate rows, deliberately not collapsed.

CROSS-SOURCE CONTRADICTION WORTH A REVIEWER'S ATTENTION. S4's Introduction states 'defibrotide has not been shown to demonstrate any significant systemic anticoagulant effects' and S4's own in vitro aPTT is read as no effect at 100 ug/mL, whereas S19 Section 13.2 records dose-dependent APTT and PT prolongation in rats and dogs at 300-4800 mg/kg/day and attributes it to 'direct effects on coagulation'. These are reconcilable by exposure (S4 tests a single fixed in vitro concentration; S19's findings are at >=6x the clinical dose on mg/m2) but the dataset should not present them as agreeing. Note also that S4 measures a mild TT prolongation, which is a coagulation effect the S4 Introduction's blanket 'no significant systemic anticoagulant effects' claim does not accommodate.

MOLECULAR-WEIGHT DISAGREEMENT. S4 reports 18.02 +/- 0.32 kDa for porcine API; S19 Section 11 specifies 14-19 kDa mean weighted MW for DEFITELIO. Consistent (S4 sits inside the label range) but measured against different calibrants (S4 used heparin fractions as SEC standards for a DNA polymer, which is itself a methodological caveat the article does not discuss).

VERBATIM QUOTE CONVENTION. JATS/SPL text contains Unicode thin/medium spaces (U+2009, U+2005) and a non-ASCII hyphen in 'inhibitor-1'; quotes are copied with those whitespace characters normalised to ordinary spaces and are otherwise character-exact. Table quotes are rendered as pipe-delimited cell sequences exactly as parsed from the source <table> markup, and where a narrative sentence corroborates the same number it is appended in square brackets so the reviewer can verify the value twice.

1. PLATELET COUNT / THROMBOCYTOPENIA - none extracted, and there was nothing to extract: a full-text keyword scan of the S19 SPL returns ZERO hits for 'platelet', and S4 never measures platelets. Had a platelet count been present it would still have been out of scope per the bundle rule (thrombocytopenia is a separate Challenge endpoint) unless tied to a cascade readout. No platelet_coag_crosstalk row exists in this bundle.

2. FIGURES 1-6 OF S4 - refused as a data source. They plot the same aPTT/TT/anti-Xa/anti-IIa/DNA/MW data already available as machine-readable tables, and the article is internally inconsistent about whether the error bars are SD (figure legends) or SEM (Results text: 'figures display the mean and standard errors'). No value was digitised from any panel.

3. PER-BATCH VALUES - refused. The source analysed 19 porcine and 9 ovine lots but publishes only pooled mean +/- SD. Individual lot values, and therefore any batch-to-batch variability row, do not exist in the text and were not reconstructed.

4. QUANTITATIVE aPTT/PT VALUES FOR THE RAT AND DOG TOXICOLOGY STUDIES (S19 13.2) - refused. The label gives direction and dose but no numbers. The dose levels are recorded; the clotting times are NOT_REPORTED. No number was back-calculated from the '>=6 times higher on a mg/m2 basis' statement, and the 6x figure is recorded as the label's own words rather than converted into an animal-to-human dose.

5. DNA CONTENT (Table 6) AND MOLECULAR WEIGHT (Table 7) OF S4 - deliberately NOT written as measurement rows. They are material-characterisation data, not coagulation readouts, so they are carried in the oligos records' identity_confirmation fields instead. Values: ovine 75.78 +/- 4.74 ug and porcine 79 +/- 6.39 ug DNA per 10 ug API; ovine 16.8 +/- 0.24 kDa and porcine 18.02 +/- 0.32 kDa.

6. S19 SECTION 12.2 QTc AND SECTION 13.1 GENOTOXICITY/FERTILITY - out of endpoint scope; no rows written.

7. 'MOST COMMON SERIOUS ADVERSE REACTIONS ... pulmonary alveolar hemorrhage (7%)' (S19 6.1) - not written as a separate row because it is the same 12 (7%) patients already captured from Table 2's Grade 4-5 column under a different label ('serious', >=5% rule). Recorded here so the omission is visible rather than silent.

8. AN ANTI-Xa / ANTI-IIa 'INCREASE vs BASELINE' DIRECTION FOR S4 - refused. The measured values (7.19-7.44) exceed the Methods' stated expectation for unexposed plasma ('below 5%'), which would suggest an increase, but no control was actually run and the units are contradictory, so asserting a direction would be inference. Those four rows carry effect_direction NOT_REPORTED.
